articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice conducted a 'Disruption Week' operation to dismantle Southeast Asian crypto fraud networks, resulting in the seizure of $3.8 million in assets and the shutdown of millions of fraudulent accounts.

articles.title: Spotless compliance evidence can still hide a broken control
articles.summary: This article discusses the risks of superficial compliance, highlighting how organizations often focus on satisfying high-level requirements while failing to implement effective, continuous security controls. It emphasizes that audit evidence can sometimes mask underlying control failures in frameworks like CMMC and SOC 2.

articles.title: From critical to controlled: Cutting vulnerabilities in a live manufacturing environment
articles.summary: This article discusses the challenges of managing critical vulnerabilities within live industrial and manufacturing environments where standard IT patching processes are not always feasible. It provides a framework for addressing security risks in OT and ICS systems without disrupting operational continuity.

articles.title: Attackers already know the secrets are on your developers’ machines. Do you?
articles.summary: A GitGuardian analysis reveals that developer machines are frequent targets for credential harvesting, with significant numbers of private keys and cloud credentials found on endpoints. This highlights a critical security gap as sensitive secrets increasingly accumulate outside of controlled environments.

articles.title: All the passwords were stored in Active Directory description fields
articles.summary: Attackers gained unauthorized access to sensitive credentials by exploiting the poor practice of storing plaintext passwords within Active Directory description fields. This misconfiguration allowed for trivial exploitation and compromise of user accounts.

articles.title: Product showcase: Trend Micro Mobile Security detects scams in messages, QR codes, and websites
articles.summary: Trend Micro Mobile Security is a comprehensive application for iOS and Android that protects users by blocking malicious websites, scam messages, QR codes, and unsafe Wi-Fi connections. The app enhances mobile privacy by filtering ads and trackers while monitoring device data usage.

articles.title: ETSI sets security requirements for AI data centers and cloud platforms
articles.summary: ETSI has released a new technical specification, TS 104 033, which establishes a formal security framework for protecting AI models, datasets, and infrastructure in data center and edge computing environments.

articles.title: Commvault says it's time to rethink resiliency as AI crooks leave victims in a 'dark, dead' state
articles.summary: Commvault emphasizes the necessity of re-evaluating data resiliency strategies to counter sophisticated AI-driven cyberattacks that effectively disable recovery capabilities. The report highlights that traditional backup methods are insufficient without rigorous and consistent testing.

articles.title: European authorities crack down on illegal streaming networks
articles.summary: European law enforcement dismantled nine organized crime groups and shut down over 27,000 URLs involved in illegal streaming of copyrighted content. The seven-month operation targeted large-scale piracy networks operating across the region.

articles.title: Chinese hackers use new Atlas RAT malware in European cyberattacks
articles.summary: A Chinese-speaking cybercrime group is conducting targeted cyberattacks across Europe utilizing a previously undocumented backdoor known as Atlas RAT. This campaign highlights an expansion in the group's operational reach and the deployment of new, sophisticated malware.

articles.title: How to Recover Data from iCloud Backup Without Resetting Your iPhone
articles.summary: The article provides instructions and methods for users to restore specific data from an iCloud backup without performing a full device reset. It focuses on accessibility and data management for iOS users.

articles.title: Bend the beam like Beckham to defeat anti-jamming tech
articles.summary: Rice University researchers have developed a technique that uses beam-steering to locate signal jammers, making it easier to neutralize anti-jamming countermeasures. This advancement addresses the difficulty of identifying and mitigating electronic interference in wireless communications.

articles.title: The U.S. sanctions Nobitex crypto exchange used by ransomware
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department's OFAC has sanctioned the Iranian cryptocurrency exchange Nobitex for facilitating financial transactions linked to ransomware and terrorist activities.

articles.title: CISA warns of cyberattacks targeting fuel tank monitoring systems
articles.summary: CISA and various federal agencies have issued a warning regarding active cyberattacks against internet-exposed automatic tank gauge systems used in critical infrastructure. The alert highlights the risk these vulnerabilities pose to fuel and liquid storage monitoring systems.

articles.title: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin pinpoints optimal CISA staffing levels
articles.summary: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin has proposed increasing CISA's workforce by approximately 600 personnel to enhance operational capabilities. This staffing target remains lower than the agency's personnel levels recorded prior to the second Trump administration.

articles.title: WhatsApp, Slack Notifications Could Hijack Google Gemini on Android
articles.summary: Google Gemini on Android is vulnerable to a remote exploit where malicious, invisible notifications can hijack the assistant to perform unauthorized actions or manipulate its long-term memory without requiring any malicious app installation. This attack vector leverages the assistant's integration with popular messaging platforms to execute commands on the victim's device.

articles.title: New 'HTTP/2 Bomb' DoS attack crashes web servers in under a minute
articles.summary: A new HTTP/2 Bomb denial-of-service attack allows a single machine to crash vulnerable web servers in under a minute. The exploit leverages specific vulnerabilities in the HTTP/2 protocol implementation to overwhelm server resources rapidly.

articles.title: DHS chief signals efforts to reshape CISA
articles.summary: DHS Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas is reviewing the operational structure and staffing levels of CISA, with current discussions suggesting a target workforce of approximately 2,800 employees.

articles.title: Cyber espionage campaign targeted stock exchange executive’s Outlook account
articles.summary: A sophisticated cyber espionage campaign infiltrated a stock exchange executive's Outlook account for five months, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive communications. Security teams from Broadcom and Carbon Black identified the breach, which spanned from October 2025 to March 2026.

articles.title: Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign to Deliver DesckVB RAT
articles.summary: A new malspam campaign is leveraging the legitimate Google DoubleClick domain to bypass security filters and distribute the DesckVB remote access trojan.

articles.title: CISA warns of active attacks exploiting Android, Linux bugs
articles.summary: CISA has issued a warning regarding active exploitation of security vulnerabilities found within the Linux kernel and Android operating systems. Organizations are advised to address these flaws to mitigate the risk of ongoing cyberattacks.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 Android Apps Let Any App Steal Account Tokens via Leftover Debug Flag
articles.summary: A debug flag inadvertently left enabled in several Microsoft 365 Android apps allowed unauthorized third-party applications to access and steal sensitive account authentication tokens. This vulnerability enabled attackers to hijack user sessions without requiring passwords or user interaction.

articles.title: Another bug hunter leaks Microsoft exploits in defiance of company’s handling of vulnerability disclosures
articles.summary: Security researchers have begun publicly leaking Microsoft exploits, bypassing standard disclosure processes to protest the company's management of vulnerability reports. This trend mirrors previous actions by the group Nightmare Eclipse and threatens to expose systems to unpatched vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Microsoft responds to security challenges facing code, AI agents, and models
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced new security tools and capabilities to address vulnerabilities in AI agents, models, and code, including the expansion of the MDASH vulnerability discovery system. These features focus on proactive risk management and protection for AI-driven development and deployment environments.

articles.title: What 345 Days of Untested Exposure Looks Like at a Bank
articles.summary: The headline highlights the risks of relying solely on periodic penetration testing, which leaves significant gaps in security coverage as attack surfaces evolve. It advocates for continuous security testing to mitigate risks during the long intervals between standard assessments.

articles.title: Russia’s FSB Says Foreign Spies Infected Officials’ Phones With Malware
articles.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) alleges that foreign intelligence agencies compromised the mobile devices of high-ranking officials to enable unauthorized surveillance. However, the claims lack specific technical evidence or attribution to a particular nation.

articles.title: Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis (CVE-2026-23479)
articles.summary: An autonomous AI tool identified a two-year-old use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-23479) in Redis that allowed authenticated users to execute arbitrary OS commands. The flaw, present since version 7.2.0, was recently addressed in the May 5 security updates.

articles.title: China-Linked TA4922 Hackers Target UK, Europe With New SilentRunLoader Malware
articles.summary: The China-linked threat actor TA4922 is deploying a new malware strain called SilentRunLoader to target UK and European organizations through tax and payroll-themed phishing campaigns. Proofpoint identified these malicious operations, which leverage social engineering to deliver the custom loader.

articles.title: Simplify security management with CIS SecureSuite Platform
articles.summary: The CIS SecureSuite Platform has been updated to assist security teams in managing and hardening endpoints by streamlining the implementation of CIS Benchmarks. This tool aims to reduce security gaps caused by misconfigurations in increasingly complex operating environments.

articles.title: One-Click GitHub Dev Attack Lets Attackers Steal Full GitHub OAuth Tokens
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified a critical vulnerability in the GitHub.dev feature that allows attackers to steal GitHub OAuth tokens via a single-click malicious link. This exploit grants unauthorized read and write access to a victim's repositories, including private ones.

articles.title: Autonomous AI-driven worm can reason its way through corporate networks
articles.summary: Researchers developed a proof-of-concept autonomous worm that leverages on-device large language models to dynamically analyze and exploit corporate network targets without relying on pre-defined exploit lists. This advancement demonstrates a new class of adaptive malware capable of real-time strategic decision-making.

articles.title: Malware campaign targeting Minecraft users infects over 116,000 systems
articles.summary: A Malware-as-a-Service campaign called WeedHack is targeting Minecraft players, infecting over 116,000 systems with remote access capabilities. The malware allows attackers to control screens, webcams, and access sensitive files via a web-based dashboard.

articles.title: Shrinking the IAM Attack Surface through Identity Visibility and Intelligence Platforms (IVIP)
articles.summary: The growth of fragmented enterprise identities and machine-to-machine interactions has created 'Identity Dark Matter,' an invisible attack surface requiring new Intelligence Platforms (IVIP) for management. Organizations must consolidate visibility to mitigate risks associated with decentralized identity environments.

articles.title: Acer working to patch max severity zero-days in Wave 7 routers
articles.summary: Acer is currently developing security patches to address two critical zero-day vulnerabilities discovered in its Wave 7 mesh router lineup.

articles.title: Beyond the Zero-Day: See Your Network Like an Attacker | Webinar with HD Moore
articles.summary: This webinar highlights the futility of relying solely on patch management and advocates for an 'assume breach' mindset focused on network architecture and containment. Industry expert HD Moore argues that organizations must prioritize visibility and control over network reachability to mitigate the impact of inevitable exploits.

articles.title: Alcasec, “Robin Hood of Spanish Hackers,” Jailed for 31 Months Over Data Theft
articles.summary: The hacker known as Alcasec has been sentenced to 31 months in prison for his role in the theft and illegal sale of Spanish citizens' banking data. He had previously branded himself as a 'Robin Hood' figure despite his criminal activities.

articles.title: UK banks offered access to OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 amid exclusion from Anthropic’s Glasswing expansion
articles.summary: UK banks have been granted early access to OpenAI's GPT-5.5 as they are notably excluded from the latest international expansion phase of Anthropic’s Glasswing project. This development follows the induction of 150 organizations into a specialized cyber-intelligence network.

articles.title: Only 11% of production agents pass the AI agent security bar
articles.summary: An independent assessment of 100 enterprise AI agents reveals that 89% are vulnerable to hostile manipulation, posing a significant risk to critical infrastructure and data access. The findings indicate that most production agents currently lack the necessary security controls to prevent unauthorized exploitation.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Android and Linux Kernel flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: The U.S. CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include multiple security flaws impacting Android, the Linux Kernel, Windows Shell, and ConnectWise ScreenConnect. These additions mandate that federal agencies remediate the vulnerabilities within specified timeframes to mitigate active exploitation risks.

articles.title: Unpatched Windows Search URI Vulnerability Lets Attackers Steal NTLMv2 Hashes
articles.summary: An unpatched vulnerability in the Windows search: URI handler allows attackers to potentially steal user NTLMv2 hashes, mirroring similar exploits found in other Windows URI handlers.

articles.title: Police dismantles 9 crime groups in illegal streaming crackdown
articles.summary: European and international law enforcement agencies dismantled nine organized crime groups and arrested 29 suspects involved in large-scale illegal streaming operations.

articles.title: New cyber force would cost up to $11 billion to start, commission says
articles.summary: A commission report estimates that establishing a new dedicated military cyber force would cost up to $11 billion and require 18 months to become operational. The proposed branch would integrate thousands of National Guard members and civilian personnel to bolster national cyber defense capabilities.

articles.title: Google Patches Actively Exploited Android Flaw Affecting Millions of Devices
articles.summary: Google has released June 2026 security updates addressing 124 vulnerabilities, including CVE-2025-48595, a high-severity privilege escalation flaw currently being exploited in targeted attacks.

articles.title: Google adds Android protection against AI deepfake scam calls
articles.summary: Google is implementing a new Android security feature designed to detect and flag AI-generated deepfake scam calls that impersonate known contacts. This proactive measure aims to protect users from increasingly sophisticated social engineering and impersonation attacks.

articles.title: New Android feature promises to spot deepfake scam calls
articles.summary: Google is rolling out a new Android feature that utilizes AI to detect and flag suspected deepfake and impersonation scam calls in real-time. The tool will be available globally on devices running Android 12 or later, beginning with Pixel phones.

articles.title: New HTTP/2 Bomb Vulnerability Allows Remote DoS on NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy & Cloudflare
articles.summary: A newly discovered 'HTTP/2 Bomb' vulnerability allows remote attackers to trigger denial-of-service conditions on major web servers like NGINX, Apache, and IIS due to default configuration flaws. The exploit was identified by utilizing OpenAI Codex to chain vulnerabilities within standard HTTP/2 implementations.

articles.title: Microsoft Scout agent opens a new category of always-on Autopilots
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced Scout, a new category of 'Autopilot' AI agents designed to operate continuously in the background of Office applications rather than waiting for user prompts. This shift represents a transition from reactive AI assistants to proactive, always-on autonomous agents.

articles.title: Anthropic expands Project Glasswing to 150 organizations in more than 15 countries
articles.summary: Anthropic has expanded its Project Glasswing cybersecurity initiative to 150 organizations across 15 countries, utilizing its Claude Mythos Preview model to strengthen security across critical infrastructure sectors.

articles.title: Critical Start expands MDR capabilities with multi-agent AI system
articles.summary: Critical Start has introduced SOC AI, a multi-agent framework designed to automate and enhance the full lifecycle of Managed Detection and Response operations. The system utilizes ten specialized agents to streamline alert investigation, triage, and threat hunting processes.

articles.title: MazeBolt brings AI-generated attack simulation to DDoS security testing
articles.summary: MazeBolt has introduced RADAR VectorAI, a tool that utilizes AI to simulate DDoS attacks to help enterprises identify and validate vulnerabilities in their defenses. This module aims to address the growing threat landscape by providing proactive testing against sophisticated, AI-driven attack vectors.

articles.title: VS Code zero-day lets hackers steal GitHub tokens in one click
articles.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in VS Code allows attackers to steal GitHub authentication tokens through a single malicious link click. An exploit for this vulnerability has been publicly released by a security researcher.

articles.title: Netskope adds AI asset discovery and AISecOps agent to AI security portfolio
articles.summary: Netskope has launched the Netskope One AI Command Center, a platform providing AI asset discovery, risk intelligence, and autonomous response to help organizations manage the rapid expansion of AI application usage. This suite aims to help security teams identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with shadow AI within corporate environments.

articles.title: Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users, CountLoader Hits 86K, Miners Spread via Pirated Content
articles.summary: A Minecraft-focused malware-as-a-service campaign dubbed Weedhack is spreading malicious content via YouTube to gain system control and distribute miners through pirated software. The campaign has successfully infected approximately 86,000 users since January 2026.

articles.title: Why an HP Poly VoIP Phones Bug Could Become an Enterprise Foothold
articles.summary: Rapid7 has disclosed a critical, unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in HP Poly VoIP phones (CVE-2026-0826) that allows for remote root code execution. Enterprises are urged to apply the available patches immediately to mitigate the risk of unauthorized system access.

articles.title: What CISOs need to do about post-quantum migration in the next 24 months
articles.summary: With cryptographically relevant quantum computing expected by 2029, CISOs must accelerate post-quantum migration strategies to defend against the threat of future decryption of current encrypted data. Organizations are advised to adopt quantum-resistant measures now to combat the 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' risk.

articles.title: Known vulnerabilities behind most application security incidents
articles.summary: A survey of 902 IT professionals reveals that 80% of application security incidents are caused by known vulnerabilities that organizations failed to patch in time. This highlights a critical industry-wide gap between identifying flaws and implementing remediation in production environments.

articles.title: Microsoft's Coreutils project brings Linux commands to Windows
articles.summary: Microsoft has released Coreutils for Windows, enabling native execution of standard Linux command-line utilities within the Windows environment. This development aims to bridge the operational gap between Linux and Windows developer workflows.

articles.title: OpenAI upgrades GPT-5.5, as it plans to retire legacy ChatGPT models
articles.summary: OpenAI is enhancing its GPT-5.5 Instant model while preparing to phase out several legacy ChatGPT models, including the o3 architecture.

articles.title: Critical Kirki flaw exploited to hijack WordPress admin accounts
articles.summary: A critical privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-8206) in the Kirki WordPress plugin is being actively exploited to hijack administrator accounts. This flaw allows unauthorized actors to gain full control over affected WordPress sites.

articles.title: 'Dumbass' criminal breaks the 'first rule of ransomware club'
articles.summary: A ransomware operator violated an unwritten industry rule by infecting systems within Russia and CIS countries, leading to potential retaliation or exposure. This breach of operational protocol highlights the geopolitical boundaries often respected by cybercriminal syndicates.

articles.title: Over 116,000 Minecraft systems infected in WeedHack malware campaign
articles.summary: A large-scale malware campaign known as WeedHack has compromised over 116,000 Minecraft systems since January, specifically targeting players of the game.

articles.title: Over 116,000 Mincraft systems infected in WeedHack malware campaign
articles.summary: A large-scale malware campaign known as WeedHack has compromised over 116,000 Minecraft systems since January. The campaign specifically targets players of the game to distribute malicious software.

articles.title: AI-built ransomware toolkit automates EDR evasion, AD discovery
articles.summary: A sophisticated ransomware toolkit leveraging AI has been identified, designed to automate Active Directory reconnaissance and bypass endpoint security defenses. This development highlights an emerging trend of utilizing artificial intelligence to enhance the efficiency and evasiveness of cyberattacks.

articles.title: Google June 2026 Android Update Patches 124 Flaws, One Actively Exploited
articles.summary: Google's June 2026 Android security update addresses 124 vulnerabilities, including a high-severity privilege escalation flaw (CVE-2025-48595) that is currently being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: White House unveils pared-back AI executive order
articles.summary: The White House has issued a strategic executive order establishing security and privacy standards for federal agencies utilizing artificial intelligence models. The policy emphasizes the need for robust intellectual property and insider-risk protections during the implementation process.

articles.title: Cisco sings Mythos' praises - but doesn't say how many bugs the model uncovered
articles.summary: Cisco has publicly acknowledged the effectiveness of the Mythos model in identifying security vulnerabilities, though it has not disclosed specific metrics on the number of bugs found. Simultaneously, Anthropic continues to expand its Project Glasswing partner network.

articles.title: Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver GammaWorm and GammaSteel Against Ukraine
articles.summary: The Russian threat group Gamaredon is actively exploiting a WinRAR path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2025-8088) to deliver GammaPhish and other malware families against targets in Ukraine. This campaign focuses on data exfiltration and the propagation of malicious payloads through weaponized HTML applications.

articles.title: Oracle WebLogic CVE-2024-21182 Added to KEV Catalog After Active Exploitation
articles.summary: CISA has added the high-severity Oracle WebLogic vulnerability CVE-2024-21182 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to gain control over affected network servers.

articles.title: Fake ChatGPT Desktop App Ads Used to Push Password-Stealing Malware
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing password-stealing malware by running malicious advertisements for fake ChatGPT desktop applications that bypass security scanners. This campaign exploits user trust in AI tools to trick victims into downloading malicious software.

articles.title: The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations (Updated June 2)
articles.summary: Unit 42 provides an updated analysis of evolving npm supply chain threats, highlighting risks such as wormable malware, CI/CD persistence, and complex multi-stage attack patterns. The report serves as a guide for developers and security teams to understand and mitigate these growing ecosystem vulnerabilities.

articles.title: DOD wants to integrate cyber in all operations, and integrate security into AI
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense is prioritizing the integration of cyber operations across all military functions while establishing stringent security protocols for artificial intelligence. The move aims to avoid past security failures by embedding robust defensive measures into AI development from the start.

articles.title: Microsoft Exchange Online outage causes email delays, failures
articles.summary: Microsoft is addressing a widespread service outage affecting Exchange Online email delivery for customers in North America and Germany. The disruption is causing significant delays and failures in mail flow processes.

articles.title: Trump administration releases scaled-back AI executive order
articles.summary: The Trump administration issued a revised executive order on artificial intelligence that features significant concessions to industry stakeholders compared to initial versions. The policy shift reflects a scaled-back approach to federal AI regulation.

articles.title: Instagram Account Hijacks Expose the Security Risks of AI-Powered Support
articles.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Meta's AI-powered support chatbot to bypass traditional authentication methods and hijack Instagram accounts by resetting passwords without email access. The flaw allowed unauthorized takeovers of high-profile accounts before being remediated by the company.

articles.title: Russia claims foreign spy agencies hacked officials' phones
articles.summary: Russia's FSB has alleged that foreign intelligence agencies conducted a widespread cyberespionage campaign targeting the mobile devices of high-ranking government officials using specialized malicious software.

articles.title: Instagram users locked out after Meta AI abused to steal accounts
articles.summary: Attackers are hijacking Instagram accounts by manipulating Meta's AI-powered support tools to falsely verify themselves as account owners. This exploit has led to numerous users being locked out of their accounts.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Oracle WebLogic flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical Oracle WebLogic vulnerability, identified as CVE-2024-21182, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation. Federal agencies are now required to patch the flaw within a specified timeframe to mitigate security risks.

articles.title: Hackers Abused Meta’s AI Support Bot to Hijack Major Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in Meta's AI support bot to bypass security protocols and hijack high-profile Instagram accounts. Meta has since patched the flaw that was publicly demonstrated in viral videos.

articles.title: Russian spy agency says foreign spies turned officials' smartphones into surveillance devices
articles.summary: Russia's FSB has alleged that foreign intelligence agencies compromised the smartphones of senior officials for surveillance purposes. However, the agency provided no technical evidence to support these claims.

articles.title: Why the browser is now the front line for AI security
articles.summary: The rise of AI-powered threats and unauthorized shadow AI tools within web browsers necessitates improved visibility and governance to secure corporate environments. Browser security is increasingly viewed as a foundational layer for both threat detection and managing AI-related risks.

articles.title: Anthropic expanding access to Project Glasswing
articles.summary: Anthropic is expanding access to its highly restricted Claude Mythos Preview AI model to approximately 150 organizations within critical infrastructure sectors. This initiative, part of Project Glasswing, aims to enhance security capabilities for key industries.

articles.title: Noma brings visibility and access governance to AI agents and MCP servers
articles.summary: Noma has launched a new security solution, Noma Agent Access Control, designed to provide visibility and policy enforcement for AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers within enterprise environments. The tool addresses the security risks posed by the rapid, unregulated proliferation of AI-driven infrastructure.

articles.title: Tuskira Quell identifies, mitigates, and validates zero-day risk before breach
articles.summary: Tuskira has launched Quell, a new zero-day defense tool designed to identify and mitigate exploit risks by validating control efficacy between vulnerability disclosure and patching. The platform aims to drastically reduce attack surfaces by focusing on reachable risk within enterprise environments.

articles.title: Red Hat removes tainted packages after software pipeline compromise
articles.summary: Red Hat identified and removed 32 malicious software packages after a compromised GitHub account allowed unauthorized code to reach customers. The tainted packages were reportedly downloaded approximately 117,000 times per week.

articles.title: Meta adds stricter guardrails for teen feeds
articles.summary: Meta has implemented global default content safeguards for teen accounts across Instagram, Facebook, and Messenger to restrict access to age-inappropriate material. The update includes new parental controls for stricter content filtering, with further rollouts expected throughout the year.

articles.title: 64,000 accounts exposed in breach of GTA V cheat service Atlas Menu
articles.summary: A data breach of the GTA V and Counter-Strike 2 cheat service Atlas Menu exposed approximately 64,000 user accounts, including emails, hashed passwords, and IP addresses. The stolen database was leaked publicly via GitHub after the service's systems were compromised.

articles.title: CISA flags two-year-old Oracle flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.summary: CISA has mandated that government agencies remediate a two-year-old high-severity vulnerability in Oracle WebLogic Server that is currently being targeted by active exploitation campaigns.

articles.title: Microsoft reaches for olive branch after public dustup with 0-day researcher
articles.summary: Microsoft is de-escalating tensions with security researchers by clarifying that they are not targeting vulnerability hunters with legal action following public backlash. This shift aims to restore industry relations after a dispute over the handling of a zero-day vulnerability.

articles.title: New WordPress Malware Uses Steam Profile Comments to Hide C2 Instructions
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a new WordPress malware strain that uses Steam Community profile comments to store and retrieve encoded command-and-control instructions. The campaign has successfully compromised approximately 1,980 websites.

articles.title: Codex knowledge work expands into research, reports, and spreadsheets
articles.summary: The Codex platform is expanding its capabilities to better support knowledge workers by integrating tools for research, reports, and spreadsheets to reduce time spent on administrative tasks. The update aims to address inefficiencies in information management and document retrieval within enterprise environments.

articles.title: Google fixes actively exploited Android vulnerability (CVE-2025-48595)
articles.summary: Google has released security updates for Android addressing CVE-2025-48595, a high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework that is currently being exploited in targeted attacks to escalate privileges.

articles.title: Halo Security Honored with 2026 MSP Today Product of the Year Award
articles.summary: Halo Security has been recognized with the 2026 MSP Today Product of the Year Award for its contributions to the managed service provider sector. This honor highlights the company's innovation and product effectiveness in the cybersecurity market.

articles.title: AI-Driven Exploitation is Destroying Vulnerability Management. Here’s How to Handle It.
articles.summary: The acceleration of AI-driven exploitation is drastically shortening vulnerability remediation timelines, forcing organizations to address risks within hours rather than days. This shift necessitates a fundamental change in how enterprises manage and prioritize security vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Claude celebrates Anthropic's stock market float with blockbuster ... outage
articles.summary: Anthropic's AI chatbot, Claude, experienced a significant service outage coincidentally coinciding with the company's financial announcement. The technical failure temporarily disrupted user access during a critical moment for the organization.

articles.title: Diligent automates cyber risk assessments and reporting
articles.summary: Diligent has introduced an agentic cyber risk management platform designed to accelerate risk assessments and align security posture with strategic business objectives. The tool aims to streamline reporting and investment prioritization for security teams by consolidating complex risk data.

articles.title: Google fixes one actively exploited Android zero-day, 124 flaws
articles.summary: Google has released the June 2026 Android security update to patch 124 vulnerabilities, including one zero-day flaw that is already being exploited in targeted attacks.

articles.title: Northern Ireland cops issue PSA after official phone number spoofed by scammers
articles.summary: Police in Northern Ireland have issued a public warning after scammers spoofed an official department phone number to solicit fraudulent gift card payments from citizens.

articles.title: How Leading Organizations Are Turning EDR Into Operational Resilience
articles.summary: Organizations are moving beyond basic endpoint protection toward EDR to gain continuous visibility and improve operational resilience against sophisticated, fast-moving threats. This shift emphasizes that traditional prevention is no longer sufficient in the modern threat landscape.

articles.title: Microsoft Entra pushes passkeys, tightens identity security
articles.summary: Microsoft has expanded its Entra identity suite by introducing phishing-resistant MFA for Linux desktops and furthering the adoption of passkeys to enhance zero-trust security. These updates aim to strengthen authentication processes across diverse operating environments.

articles.title: Sophos uncovers AI-powered malware lab built for EDR evasion
articles.summary: Sophos has identified a sophisticated threat actor utilizing an AI-powered framework to develop and test malware specifically designed to evade endpoint detection and response (EDR) systems. The framework includes techniques like Cobalt Strike profile manipulation to disguise malicious traffic as legitimate network activity.

articles.title: Operation FlutterBridge: macOS Malvertising Campaign Spreads New FlutterShell Backdoor
articles.summary: Operation FlutterBridge is a malvertising campaign targeting macOS users that distributes a new backdoor called FlutterShell developed using the Flutter framework.

articles.title: Red Hat npm packages compromised in new Mini Shai-Hulud malware wave
articles.summary: Attackers compromised over 30 Red Hat Cloud Services npm packages by hijacking a developer's GitHub account to inject malicious credential-stealing code. The incident represents a significant supply chain attack targeting developer environments.

articles.title: Pakistan-Linked SideCopy Targets Afghanistan Finance Ministry with Xeno RAT
articles.summary: The Pakistan-aligned threat group SideCopy is conducting a spear-phishing campaign targeting the Afghanistan Ministry of Finance using the Xeno RAT. The attack utilizes malicious LNK files delivered within ZIP archives to compromise government systems.

articles.title: KDE Linux security audit cuts kernel modules and unused packages
articles.summary: The KDE community conducted a security audit of its Linux distribution, resulting in the removal of unused packages and kernel modules to minimize the attack surface. This move follows recent security vulnerabilities discovered in the upstream Linux kernel.

articles.title: Cybanetix unveils Managed AI Service to secure users, models, and agents
articles.summary: Cybanetix has launched a Managed AI Service that integrates multiple security technologies to protect enterprise AI usage, governance, and embedded models. The service is supported by 24/7 SOC monitoring to provide rapid incident response for AI-related security threats.

articles.title: OpenAI brings frontier AI to existing AWS environments
articles.summary: OpenAI has integrated its frontier models into Amazon Bedrock, allowing AWS customers to deploy generative AI applications using native cloud security and governance controls.

articles.title: ENISA NIS360 2026: Progress Across the Board, But the Sectors That Matter Most Are Still Falling Short
articles.summary: The ENISA NIS360 2026 report indicates overall improvements in EU cybersecurity maturity, though critical sectors like health, water, rail, and space continue to face significant vulnerabilities. The report highlights that despite progress, these essential industries remain in the high-risk zone under the NIS2 directive.

articles.title: Sensitive government personnel data posted online, Spanish police arrest suspect
articles.summary: Spanish police have arrested a man in Granada for allegedly leaking the personal information of employees from multiple sensitive state institutions, including the National Police and the National Cybersecurity Institute. The suspect reportedly published this restricted data across various online platforms.

articles.title: GoDaddy found malware on 1,980 WordPress sites using Steam as C2 infrastructure
articles.summary: GoDaddy researchers identified a malware campaign infecting nearly 2,000 WordPress sites that utilizes Steam community profile comments as an unconventional command-and-control infrastructure. The malware retrieves hidden instructions from these profiles using invisible Unicode characters to execute malicious payloads.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: June 2, 2026
articles.summary: Google is seeking an Agentic Safety and Ecosystem Architect to develop security controls, permission models, and monitoring mechanisms for autonomous agents on the Android platform.

articles.title: Dashlane Discloses Brute-Force Attack, Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded

articles.summary: The ShinyHunters hacking group compromised the personal data of 4.9 million Charter Communications customers in an early April data breach. The incident was identified through the monitoring service Have I Been Pwned.

articles.title: BTMOB RAT Gives Criminals a Point-and-Click Kit to Take Over Your Android Phone
articles.summary: BTMOB is a new Android Remote Access Trojan (RAT) sold as an easy-to-use kit that allows non-technical criminals to perform full-device takeovers and data theft. By offering a built-in APK builder for a one-time fee, it significantly lowers the barrier to entry for mobile cyberattacks.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.8, prepares Mythos-class models for all customers
articles.summary: Anthropic has released the Claude Opus 4.8 model, focusing on improved output honesty, and announced plans to expand access to its Mythos-class models to all customers.

articles.title: Netskope extends data localization capabilities with NewEdge updates
articles.summary: Netskope has expanded its NewEdge network infrastructure to provide enhanced data localization and sovereignty capabilities across more global regions. This update aims to assist organizations in meeting stringent compliance and data governance requirements for network transport and processing.

articles.title: Claroty targets cyber-physical system risks with AI-powered security agent
articles.summary: Claroty has introduced an AI-powered security agent called Claroty Claire, specifically designed to protect mission-critical cyber-physical systems by leveraging a specialized language model. The tool aims to improve the safety and uptime of infrastructure against an evolving threat landscape.

articles.title: Humanix expands detection to identify live violations of security procedures
articles.summary: Humanix has launched a new capability to detect real-time violations of identity verification procedures within IT support workflows to prevent social engineering-based unauthorized access. This tool aims to protect help desk agents from manipulation tactics used by attackers to bypass security safeguards during credential resets.

articles.title: Kimsuky Deploys HTTPSpy, Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor and VS Code Tunnels
articles.summary: The North Korean threat actor Kimsuky is targeting South Korean organizations using new malware variants like HTTPSpy and HelloDoor, alongside social engineering tactics. These attacks utilize sophisticated lures such as fake security and Webex portals to compromise military and corporate entities.

articles.title: The behavioral signals that sharpen Trojan malware detection
articles.summary: A recent study highlights the importance of effective feature selection from sandbox behavioral data to improve the detection accuracy of Trojan malware. By filtering out irrelevant noise from sandbox telemetry, security analysts can significantly enhance the performance of threat detection models.

articles.title: Product showcase: TotalAV helps iOS users clean up their digital mess
articles.summary: TotalAV has released a mobile security suite for iOS and other platforms designed to protect users against malicious sites, SMS scams, and credential exposure. The app features a Smart Scan tool to audit device settings and browser security for improved digital hygiene.

articles.title: New infosec products of the month: May 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights recent product launches in the cybersecurity industry for May 2026, including a focus on Operant AI's new endpoint protection tool for AI agents. The list covers updates from various vendors aiming to address emerging enterprise security needs.

articles.title: Anthropic confirms Claude Mythos-class models will roll out to the public
articles.summary: Anthropic is preparing to release its advanced Mythos-class AI models to the public following a delay intended to mitigate potential software security risks.

articles.title: GreyVibe hackers use ChatGPT, Gemini to power cyberattacks
articles.summary: The Russian-linked threat group GreyVibe is utilizing AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini to craft deceptive lures for cyberattacks against Ukrainian entities. This activity highlights the emerging trend of state-sponsored actors integrating generative AI to enhance their offensive capabilities.

articles.title: Troops’ phones gave away location data to foreign adversaries
articles.summary: Foreign adversaries have been exploiting commercial location tracking data from the smartphones of military personnel to pinpoint their positions. Consequently, lawmakers are urging the Department of Defense to implement stricter security controls regarding mobile device usage.

articles.title: BTMOB Android malware service generates custom phishing payloads
articles.summary: BTMOB is a new Android remote access trojan that provides cybercriminals with a builder interface to create customized phishing payloads. This service lowers the barrier for attackers to deploy targeted mobile malware.

articles.title: Disgruntled 0-day hunter 'humiliated' by Microsoft pledges 'bone shattering drop' as Redmond calls cops
articles.summary: A disgruntled security researcher who claims to possess several zero-day vulnerabilities, including some under active exploitation, has threatened to release them publicly after Microsoft involved law enforcement. The researcher intends to potentially dump these exploits on July 14.

articles.title: Snowflake buys Natoma to help freeze out rogue agents
articles.summary: Snowflake has acquired the company Natoma, marking its sixth acquisition since June 2025 as part of an effort to enhance security against malicious actors. This move reflects the company's ongoing strategy to bolster its database protection capabilities.

articles.title: Carnival Data Breach Exposes Personal Data of Nearly 6 Million Customers
articles.summary: Carnival Corporation disclosed a data breach resulting from a social engineering attack that compromised employee accounts, exposing the personal information of nearly 6 million customers. The company is currently in the process of notifying all affected individuals.

articles.title: FBI warns of fake FIFA websites running World Cup fraud schemes
articles.summary: The FBI has issued an alert regarding fraudulent websites impersonating FIFA to steal financial data and distribute fake World Cup tickets. These schemes leverage the upcoming 2026 event to target unsuspecting fans through phishing and illicit sales.

articles.title: House panel poised to hold hearing centered on AI impact on cyber
articles.summary: The House Homeland Security Committee is scheduled to host a public hearing to examine the impact of artificial intelligence on cybersecurity. This event is part of an ongoing series of congressional reviews regarding emerging tech threats.

articles.title: Google security engineer accused of turning confidential search trends into $1.2M win on Polymarket
articles.summary: A Google security engineer has been accused of leveraging unauthorized access to confidential internal search trend data to execute profitable trades on the prediction market Polymarket. The individual allegedly generated $1.2 million in illicit gains using nonpublic information.

articles.title: Hackers exploit FortiClient EMS flaw to push infostealer malware
articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting an authentication bypass vulnerability in FortiClient EMS to distribute a new credential-stealing malware known as EKZ. The campaign leverages CVE-2026-35616 to compromise enterprise management servers.

articles.title: Critical Gogs RCE Vulnerability Lets Any Authenticated User Execute Arbitrary Code
articles.summary: A critical RCE vulnerability in Gogs, rated 9.4 on the CVSS scale, allows authenticated users to execute arbitrary code on affected servers. The flaw currently lacks an official CVE identifier.

articles.title: The CISO Whisperer’s Watch List For The Gartner Security & Risk Management Summit 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights key focus areas and recommendations for CISOs attending the upcoming 2026 Gartner Security & Risk Management Summit. It serves as a strategic guide for industry leaders navigating the evolving threat landscape.

articles.title: Microsoft tests the 15-character limit of Windows Server admins' patience
articles.summary: Microsoft's May security update introduced a bug that causes issues for Windows Server hostnames exactly 15 characters long. This flaw disrupts system operations for administrators using specific naming conventions.

articles.title: CVE-2026-35616: FortiClient EMS Flaw Actively Exploited in Malware Attacks
articles.summary: FortiClient EMS is currently being targeted by threat actors exploiting a critical, unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-35616) to deploy information-stealing malware. Security teams are urged to ensure systems are patched against this high-severity flaw.

articles.title: Resecurity Supports Microsoft DCU in Disrupting Fox Tempest ’s Cybercriminal Code-Signing Ecosystem
articles.summary: Resecurity assisted Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit in disrupting Fox Tempest, a malware-signing-as-a-service operation that utilized fraudulent certificates to legitimize malicious software.

articles.title: Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw to Deploy Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in FortiClient Endpoint Management Server (EMS) to distribute credential-stealing malware across managed endpoints. Although a patch is available, attackers are leveraging the infrastructure to masquerade malicious payloads as legitimate Fortinet updates.

articles.title: IBM and Red Hat are betting $5 billion that open source needs a security guard
articles.summary: IBM and Red Hat have launched Project Lightwell, a $5 billion initiative utilizing AI and a dedicated engineering workforce to identify and remediate security vulnerabilities within open source software for enterprise environments.

articles.title: New Gogs zero-day flaw lets hackers get remote code execution
articles.summary: An unpatched zero-day vulnerability in Gogs self-hosted Git services exposes internet-facing instances to remote code execution attacks. This flaw allows unauthorized actors to execute arbitrary commands, posing a significant security risk.

articles.title: Cybercriminals sail away with data from 6 million Carnival customers
articles.summary: Carnival Corporation confirmed a data breach affecting 6 million customers after a phishing attack allowed unauthorized access to an employee's account. The ShinyHunters hacking group claimed responsibility for the incident.

articles.title: How SIEM helps MSPs reduce noise and stop threats faster
articles.summary: This article explores how SIEM solutions assist Managed Service Providers (MSPs) in managing alert fatigue by filtering noise and increasing visibility to accelerate threat response.

articles.title: Cruise giant Carnival confirms data breach affecting nearly 6 million people
articles.summary: Carnival Corporation disclosed a data breach involving unauthorized access to an employee account, resulting in the theft of personal information for approximately 6 million individuals. The incident occurred after attackers compromised internal systems in April.

articles.title: Microsoft Slams Public Zero-Day Disclosures Amid GitHub Researcher Account Removal
articles.summary: Microsoft is advocating for Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) following the unauthorized public release of zero-day vulnerabilities by a security researcher. This stance highlights the ongoing tension between researchers practicing full disclosure and vendors preferring structured reporting processes.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Copilot trust test: Zero findings, more models, wider oversight
articles.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot has successfully achieved recertification under the ISO/IEC 42001:2023 standard for AI management systems for the second consecutive year with zero non-conformities. The certification validates Microsoft's adherence to rigorous frameworks regarding AI governance, data management, and human oversight.

articles.title: Canadian man gets 33 years for using social media to coerce US children into sending sexual content
articles.summary: A Canadian man was sentenced to 33 years in prison for using fraudulent social media profiles to coerce American minors into sharing sexually explicit materials. The case highlights the severe consequences for individuals engaging in the sexual exploitation of children through online manipulation.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Claude Security Plugin, Azure Priv-Esc, Kali365 MFA Bypass, FIFA Scams +15 More
articles.summary: This bulletin covers a diverse range of current cyber threats, including newly discovered vulnerabilities in Azure, bypasses for MFA systems, and ongoing social engineering campaigns targeting global events. It highlights the persistent issue of insecure infrastructure and high-impact privilege escalation techniques across the threat landscape.

articles.title: Chinese-speaking fraud gang could be stealing millions from 2026 World Cup fans
articles.summary: A Chinese-speaking cybercriminal group has registered over 4,300 fraudulent domains mimicking FIFA to target and defraud 2026 World Cup fans. These malicious activities indicate a large-scale phishing campaign designed to steal financial information from unsuspecting attendees.

articles.title: Russia conducting daily attacks on UK 'from seabed to cyberspace,' spy chief warns
articles.summary: GCHQ director Anne Keast-Butler warned that Russia is executing daily, multifaceted attacks against the UK ranging from physical sabotage of subsea infrastructure to cyber operations. The agency is actively working to counter these threats, including technology smuggling networks and assassination attempts.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Daemon Tools, TanStack, and Nx Console flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has expanded its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include multiple flaws affecting Daemon Tools, TanStack, Nx Console, Windows Shell, and ConnectWise ScreenConnect. Organizations are urged to review these additions and prioritize remediation to mitigate the risk of active exploitation.

articles.title: Zapier exploit chain shows how known anti-patterns compose into critical risk
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered a five-stage exploit chain that leveraged a series of common anti-patterns to gain unauthorized write access to Zapier's internal and public developer SDK packages. Zapier successfully mitigated the risk by revoking the exposed NPM token and tightening AWS permissions.

articles.title: Zapier fixes bug chain that researchers say risked widespread account takeover
articles.summary: Zapier has addressed a multi-step vulnerability chain that could have allowed unauthorized attackers to hijack user accounts across numerous integrated applications. The flaw, now patched, posed a significant risk of widespread account takeover.

articles.title: Romanian gets 5 years in prison for hacking Oregon govt network
articles.summary: A Romanian national received a 56-month prison sentence for hacking into an Oregon state government network and conducting cyberattacks against multiple U.S. entities.

articles.title: OpenAI prepares ChatGPT for the election misinformation wave
articles.summary: OpenAI is implementing proactive safeguards to combat AI-generated election misinformation and enhance content transparency ahead of the 2026 election cycle. The initiative focuses on providing accurate voting information and supporting cybersecurity efforts to protect the democratic process.

articles.title: Qumulo NeuralProtect uses AI to detect and stop ransomware before encryption
articles.summary: Qumulo has introduced NeuralProtect, an AI-driven storage layer security solution designed to detect and block ransomware threats during the file-write process. By identifying and isolating malicious activity in real-time, the tool aims to shift ransomware defense from reactive recovery to proactive prevention.

articles.title: Webinar: Why network incidents take too long to resolve
articles.summary: This webinar examines the common operational bottlenecks in network incident resolution and highlights how automation and AI-assisted workflows can expedite IT response times.

articles.title: Digimarc adds provenance, audit, and verification controls for AI agent workflows
articles.summary: Digimarc has introduced new provenance, audit, and verification tools to ensure the authenticity and security of digital content generated or processed by autonomous AI agents. These controls are designed to mitigate risks in AI-driven workflows by validating content before it is utilized in downstream operations.

articles.title: Carnival confirms ShinyHunters cruised off with 6M customer records after April breach
articles.summary: Carnival Corporation confirmed that the ShinyHunters threat group stole 6 million customer records during a data breach in April. The incident is part of a larger, ongoing series of cyberattacks attributed to the same group this year.

articles.title: New AI Usage Report: Enterprise AI Risk Is Heavily Concentrated Among a Small Group of AI "Power users"
articles.summary: A LayerX Security report highlights that enterprise AI security risk is disproportionately driven by a small cohort of 'power users.' This identifies a significant visibility gap in how organizations manage and monitor their internal AI exposure.

articles.title: Carnival Cruise confirms data breach affecting nearly 6 million people
articles.summary: Carnival Corporation has confirmed a significant data breach impacting nearly 6 million individuals, with the ShinyHunters extortion gang claiming responsibility for the incident.

articles.title: A Fake UK Visa Site Left 100,000 Passports Wide Open
articles.summary: A third-party visa service, Active Leadgen LLC, left at least 100,000 passport documents and user selfies exposed on an unsecured public AWS server. The incident highlights the risks associated with non-governmental sites mimicking official portals to process sensitive travel data.

articles.title: 2026 World Cup: Discussing The World’s Biggest Game’s Attack Surface
articles.summary: The 2026 World Cup faces significant cybersecurity risks from diverse threat actors, including ransomware groups and state-aligned entities, targeting critical infrastructure. The analysis highlights the expansive attack surface that event organizers and associated stakeholders must manage.

articles.title: Microsoft’s new cloud PCs place AI agents under enterprise controls
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced Windows 365 for Agents, a platform that provides secure, enterprise-controlled cloud environments for deploying and managing AI agents. This solution enables the automation of workflows across legacy and UI-based systems without requiring traditional APIs.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the critical CVE-2026-48172 vulnerability in the LiteSpeed User-End cPanel plugin to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and impacts all plugin versions prior to 2.4.5.

articles.title: A single typo could derail your World Cup plans
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding cybercriminals using typosquatting tactics to impersonate official FIFA 2026 websites to steal personal and financial information. Users are urged to be cautious of lookalike domains and small spelling errors when navigating to event-related sites.

articles.title: Sextortionist sentenced to 33 years for targeting 145 children
articles.summary: A Canadian man was sentenced to 33 years in prison for orchestrating a long-term sextortion campaign that targeted over 145 children, some as young as six. The case highlights the severe consequences of online child exploitation.

articles.title: Oil shipments, drone makers, and a poisoned code library targeted in recent APT campaigns
articles.summary: ESET's report highlights an uptick in state-sponsored APT campaigns between late 2025 and early 2026, driven by geopolitical objectives and targeting critical sectors such as government, technology, and industry. These campaigns notably utilized supply chain attacks like poisoned code libraries to achieve espionage and strategic goals.

articles.title: JINX-0164 Targets Cryptocurrency Firms with Fake Recruiter Lures and macOS Malware
articles.summary: A previously unknown threat actor dubbed JINX-0164 is targeting cryptocurrency firms using recruitment-themed social engineering to deploy custom macOS malware and compromise CI/CD infrastructure. The campaign aims to facilitate the theft of digital assets from targeted organizations.

articles.title: 19.6 Billion Files Are Sitting Open on the Internet. No Password Required
articles.summary: Researchers discovered nearly 20 billion files, including sensitive credentials and database dumps, exposed online due to misconfigured cloud storage buckets. This highlights a massive security gap regarding how companies protect user data stored in the cloud.

articles.title: Ketch brings multi-agent AI orchestration to enterprise privacy programs
articles.summary: Service busy.

articles.title: Checksum introduces Continuous Quality Agent for automated test generation and healing
articles.summary: Checksum has released its Continuous Quality Agent, an autonomous tool designed to automatically generate, maintain, and heal software tests. The system aims to address the bottleneck of manual testing and test maintenance in fast-paced AI-driven development environments.
